html:
Ingapirca is the largest Inca ruin in Ecuador, in the southern highlands near Cuenca. Its oval Temple of the Sun was built of finely fitted stone in the late 1400s.

The site was first a holy place of the Cañari people. When the Inca under Topa Inca conquered them, they built a temple and storehouses there and made it a stop on the Inca road to the north. The Cañari resisted Inca rule and later sided with the Spanish against it.

The nearby Inca city of Tomebamba, birthplace of Huayna Capac, was destroyed in the Inca civil war, so Ingapirca is the best surviving trace of Inca rule in Ecuador. It shows how the Inca joined local shrines to their own sun cult.
sum: Ingapirca is the largest Inca ruin in Ecuador, in the southern highlands near Cuenca. Its oval Temple of the Sun was built of finely fitted stone in the late 1400s.
